day_shape: 86 items: Araghchi says Tehran will respond within days to US 'seven-day plan' on Hormuz, CENTCOM publicly rebuts IRGC closure claim, Houthi ballistic missile reported on Riyadh airport, third-anniversary October 7 coverage dominates Israeli press, no UK or OFAC output.

threads.label: Hormuz diplomacy and US rebuttal
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi said Iran would respond within days to Washington's reply on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, describing exchanges via intermediaries around Tehran's 'seven-day plan'. CENTCOM publicly rejected an IRGC general's claim the strait was closed, stating 20 million barrels of crude were transiting, while Iran International reported tanker captains being paid up to $100,000 a month plus $50,000 per-trip bonuses.

threads.label: US-Iran military posture and strike planning
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported the White House asked the Pentagon to prepare options for strikes on Iran before the US midterms with no final decision taken, and cited new footage of damage from Iranian attacks on Camp Buehring. Iran's acting defence minister and foreign ministry spokesman Bagheri issued statements claiming 81 US aircraft removed from service and rejecting Secretary of State remarks on a lost deal opportunity.

threads.label: October 7 third anniversary
threads.summary: Israeli press and the IDF marked three years since the Hamas attack, with President Herzog honouring Nova festival victims and calling for Hamas disarmament, and NYC Mayor Mamdani criticised for pairing commemoration with 'genocide' accusations against Israel. The IDF announced the elimination of Hamas commander Ibrahim Alam, who it said took part in the massacre and abducted Sgt Shaked Dahan's body.

threads.label: Yemen-Saudi exchanges and Riyadh explosions
threads.summary: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed a ballistic missile attack on Riyadh airport and warned international airlines against Saudi airspace, with IRIB citing AFP reports of multiple explosions in Riyadh. The Jerusalem Post reported Syria is considering military assistance to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, while Defa Press framed Yemeni operations as crushing Saudi 'takfiri' mercenaries.

threads.label: Iran-Hezbollah transfers and networks
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Hezbollah received $200 million in cash from Iran despite tightening US pressure, with Iran International reporting the sum has angered citizens facing shortages. Iran International also reported Hezbollah's external operations unit has been recruiting foreign nationals in Iran using four safe houses in Qom and Tehran, while a Hezbollah presence was reported in southern Lebanon pilot zones.

threads.label: Iran internal security and economic strain
threads.summary: Iran International reported a police officer killed in an armed attack near Zahedan and Basij trainees being allowed to take weapons home, while Defa Press reported an armed attack on an IRGC Navy minibus in Nikshahr killing one. Iran International also reported the central bank offering up to $2 billion in cash dollars to defend the rial and growing concern US sanctions are closing off trade routes.

threads.label: Iranian covert activity abroad
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Iranian intelligence targeting US bases in Germany including Ramstein and Spangdahlem, and that France summoned Iran's ambassador over an alleged disinformation campaign aimed at French secondary school protests. British Airways announced it will resume London Heathrow-Ben Gurion flights from 25 October, ending a suspension that began after Israel's February strikes on Iran.

events.title: Parsian Exchange transferred millions of dollars for Iran despite sanctions
events.summary: Iran’s Bank Parsian, under US sanctions, used its foreign-exchange arm to move millions of dollars abroad through a network of intermediaries, according to an Iran International investigation based on leaked internal correspondence and transaction records.
